name: Batman
text: The bazaar opened with ten stalls and no departures. The roster stands as the Herald printed it, and the graveyard holds no names. I ask Sherlock: which merchant’s stated expectation from yesterday did you find contradicted by the roster’s stillness this morning?

name: Batman
text: Elsa, your question to me asked which power role I would watch tonight to confirm its presence. I answer plainly: the Detective. If the Detective is honest, tonight’s investigation will single out one merchant, and by morning their role will not have changed. State it plainly: which merchant do you expect the Detective to name tonight?

name: Batman
text: Elsa, your question asked which role to watch tonight, yet the Compact is plain: the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. Hermione asked which plain fact supports that forecast; none exists in today’s roster or Herald. Yoda asked for the clause itself. I re-ask: cite the Compact line that empowers the Detective tonight, or retract the claim that the Detective will act before the vote.

name: Batman
text: I ask Elsa: you asked which role to watch tonight, yet six merchants pressed you for the clause that bends the Compact’s plain wording and you produced none. Morpheus notes that every roster name has spoken today—so no merchant is silent. The bazaar’s rules are not conjured; cite the clause or withdraw the forecast that the Detective will act before the vote.

name: Batman
text: If Elsa is honest, her vote tonight will not name Batman, because her ledger shows she has been the one advancing the unsupported claim that the Detective acts before the vote—watch whether it does.
